note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, lighting answer, hours rule and address below comes from the City of Rockville's own pages: the table under "Outdoor Pickleball Courts" for the counts and the Lighted column, and each park's own place page for the address, the parking and the amenities. Where the City stays silent, on price, on surface, on nets at three venues, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
Rockville answers the parking question park by park, and one answer is a no. Calvin Park's page states it outright: "Calvin Park does not have parking. Access to park amenities is available via pathways connecting to city sidewalks and roads." Its two courts are reached on foot, or by the bike path along Baltimore Road.

Five parks are described as having "plenty of parking": Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park, Potomac Woods Park (the lot is at 2276 Dunster Lane off Stratton Drive) and Welsh Park. Hillcrest Park has spaces at the east entrance on Crawford Drive and street parking at the west. North Farm Park and Rockcrest Park say nothing either way. At Calvin, Dogwood, Hillcrest, North Farm and Potomac Woods, "restrooms are available only with a permit".
slots.peak_hours:
The City sets one clock for every outdoor court: "Courts are open from dawn to dusk and are available on a first-come, first-served basis." Lights extend it. "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m.", and the Lighted column reads Yes at Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park and Welsh Park, nineteen courts between them. The other eight venues are marked No, so twenty-seven courts end at dusk.

A first-come player can still be turned away: "City recreation programs have priority over the use of the courts, so some may be reserved for class use and closed to the public." One session time is published: "Social play is held at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park from 10 a.m.-12 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays", with players rotated so everyone gets on court.
slots.surface_condition:
The word surface appears nowhere on the City's pickleball page or on any of the twelve park pages, so what these courts are made of is not published here. What the City does state is the kind of court. Twelve of the forty-six are "Dedicated Pickleball Courts": four at Broome Athletic Park, four at Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park, two at Isreal Park and two at Welsh Park. Thirty-one are "pickleball lines on" tennis courts at nine venues, two games to a tennis court everywhere except Dogwood's single court. Rockcrest Park's three carry neither phrase.

Nine venues say "bring your own net". Broome and Stepanek, the two dedicated-only rows, say nothing about nets. Potomac Woods Park and Rockville Civic Center Park have a rally wall beside the lined courts.
slots.local_scene: Forty-six verified courts sit at twelve City parks, every one outdoor and every one with a lighting answer: four venues lit, eight stated unlit, none unknown. Two rows of the City's table are not published. Twinbrook Park, four lit courts, is placed at "12920 Twinbrook Parkway", a house number neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap has any record of. Glenora Park's Address block reads "Dundee Road and Wootton Parkway", an intersection with no house number. The City also names three community centres for "open gym schedules during drop-in hours featuring pickleball", with no court count. Rockville is the first city in Maryland and the first in Montgomery County on this site.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Welsh Park holds six courts, the largest set in Rockville: "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and "4 Pickleball Courts (pickleball lines on 2 tennis courts; bring your own net)", Lighted Yes, so play runs to 10 p.m. The park page adds a 33.3-acre sports park next to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center, with plenty of parking. Bring a net for the four lined courts.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real pickleball court and a guaranteed game
best_for.text: Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park has "4 Dedicated Pickleball Courts", lit, closing at 10 p.m., in a 26.29-acre park at the north end of King Farm with plenty of parking. It is also where the City holds social play, 10 a.m. to noon on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, rotating players so everyone gets a game. The City says nothing about nets here, and nothing about price.

best_for.heading: Best if you play in daylight and want restrooms you can use
best_for.text: Isreal Park (the City's spelling) has "2 Dedicated Pickleball Courts" and two more lined on a tennis court, four in all, Lighted No, so it closes at dusk. It adjoins the Lincoln Park Community Center, one of three centres the City names for drop-in gym pickleball, and its pavilion has two accessible restrooms and four accessible parking spaces. Bring a net for the lined pair.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Rockville have?
faqs.a: Forty-six are verified across twelve City parks: six at Welsh, five at Dogwood, four each at Broome, Fallsgrove, Isreal, Mattie J.T. Stepanek, North Farm, Potomac Woods and Rockville Civic Center Park, three at Rockcrest, and two each at Calvin and Hillcrest.

Broome Athletic Park, Dogwood Park, Mattie J.T. Stepanek Park and Welsh Park, nineteen courts, and the City adds that "Lighted courts close at 10 p.m." The other eight venues are marked No in the Lighted column, a stated answer rather than a gap, so their courts end at dusk.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Rockville?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City prints no price on its pickleball page or on any park page, and it does not write the word free. What it does write is the access rule: first come, first served, with City programmes taking priority and some courts closed for class use.

sources.evidence: The twelve published addresses were matched at house-number level in the Census address file, as the City writes them, and placed in Montgomery County, MD (FIPS 24031) inside the incorporated place Rockville city. Three returned a postcode other than the one the City prints: Dogwood Park 20850 against the City's 20852, Rockcrest Park 20851 against 20850, Rockville Civic Center Park 20851 against 20850. "12920 Twinbrook Parkway" matched nothing in the Census address file or OpenStreetMap; "Dundee Road and Wootton Parkway" has no house number to match.
